newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian police hopes rise in missing children hunt.
newsitem.headline: Belgian police hopes rise in missing children hunt.

text.p: Belgian police said on Sunday they were on the verge of a breakthrough in their three-day-old search of a disused mine complex that could contain traces of a paedophile gang's victims.

"We have found a third shaft which is close to the zone that interests us...Tomorrow we aim to confirm that it leads to the gallery where we believe there was a hiding place (for children)," Gendarmerie Major Marcel Guissard told a news conference.

Belgian police began searching the mine in Jumet, near the south Belgian town of Charleroi, on Friday. It is part of a complex that was searched in October on information provided by Marc Dutroux, chief suspect in the child sex abuse scandal that has gripped the country since August.
But the scale of the complex -- the mine, closed in 1964, has an estimated 19 entrances and 20 separate underground galleries -- has frustrated the team of 80 investigators.
On Saturday, two entrances were uncovered, but work on excavating them was abandoned due to flooding in one and the ruinous state of the other.
On Sunday, however, Michel Bourlet, the Neufchateau-based prosecutor leading the Dutroux inquiry, said he remained convinced the mine would reveal dark secrets.
"We are not necessarily looking for bodies but a place where Dutroux may have hidden children...In October we were perhaps 100 metres away from where this hiding place was," Bourlet said.
Dutroux owned a caravan and land at the site and is known to have spent time there.
"I repeat, it is not impossible that we will find bodies but we have no information to permit us to hypothesise about the their possible identity," Guissard said.
Dutroux and several alleged accomplices have been detained since August after two young girls were rescued alive from a secret dungeon in a house he owned.
The bodies of four other girls were later found buried at properties connected to Dutroux and an acquaintance, Bernard Weinstein, whose body was also found.
Bourlet said they had returned to the Jumet mine complex after re-examining the testimonies made in September by Dutroux and girlfriend Michelle Martin, who is also being detained
Police are searching for at least seven missing children.
On Tuesday, police charged another man in connection with the abduction in 1992 in Brussels of a nine-year-old Moroccan girl, Loubna Benaissa.
